notes: CLI invocation needs -n appmixer:ai:mistral on auth login: the ai/ namespace uses
module.json and appmixer-cli/src/am-lib.js:159 lstats service.json unguarded.
Ordered cheapest-and-most-informative first. ListModels runs first because it
provides the live model ids every later step depends on. Steps marked billable:true
consume Mistral inference credits; all are sized to be trivially small (short
prompts, one embedding input, a 2-page PDF, a few seconds of audio).
Highest-risk components (spec uncertainty, must be confirmed against live
responses rather than docs): CreateSpeech (model id, default voice_id, and whether
the API returns base64 audio_data or a raw binary body) and Moderate (exact
category key names).
Known CLI harness gaps to expect, NOT connector defects: appmixer-test-component.js
mocks saveFileStream as Buffer.from(stream) and provides no staticCache/lock. That
affects CreateSpeech (file output) and the caching path in ListModels; both are
verified via E2E flows in step 3b instead.
CLI RUN RESULT: 10/10 components pass. Seven real defects were found and fixed, five
of which only a live call could surface (Moderate category names, the CreateSpeech
voice parameter, its missing model default, its unusable UUID input, and the thin
ListModels schema).
Observed rate limits from Mistral response headers: 100 requests/minute and 100000
tokens/minute. quota.js is set to 60/minute, a deliberate margin below that.
Model dropdowns are now filtered by capability rather than listing all 56 models:
chat 37, vision 32, ocr 7, transcription 2, speech 2, moderation 1, embedding 4.
Embedding models are identified by carrying no capability flag at all.
REVIEW FIXES (PR #1218), E2E RE-RUN NEEDED: the documents-and-audio flow now downloads
the audio and the PDF into file storage first and drives CreateTranscription and
ExtractDocumentText through a real fileId, so the multipart / base64-data-URI branches
the CLI harness cannot mock are finally exercised; both downloaded files are removed
after AfterAll. The chat flow's three deep static-outPort variables were rewritten as
g_jsonPath modifiers. appmixer e2e validate now passes all 27 validators, but the flows
have not been executed since.

notes: The first run of all four flows printed PASSED while two of them recorded ZERO
assertions. Two authoring bugs caused it, both fixed:
1. A regex assertion reads its pattern from the clause field `regex`, not
`expected` (utils/test/Assert switches the two on assertion type). With
`expected` the pattern is undefined and the assertion matches anything.
2. ProcessE2EResults must read `$.<afterAll>.out`. In the two flows with a
RemoveFile cleanup after AfterAll it was reading the cleanup component's own
output ({fileId}), so the assert roll-up never reached the store.
Import must use --no-validate: the local rule static-outport-deep-path resolves an
outPort option by its first path segment only, so it wrongly rejects the dotted
option values this connector declares (choices.message.content,
categories.jailbreaking). The server offers exactly those paths - it rejected the
shortened form the rule asked for. Run `appmixer e2e validate` separately; the
three static-outport-deep-path findings there are that known false positive.
